column1: # steering group, build A (note 0009 D7.1, B08). Builder A, 2026-11-20.
# Sources: EasyMesh through the usp-spec MCP server (doc easymesh): §3.1.2 Conventions (bit/byte order per [2] = IEEE
#   1905.1, multi-octet integers big-endian unless otherwise stated; reserved objects set to zero by the sender,
#   ignored by the recipient), §17.2.20 Table 42, §17.2.29 Table 51, §17.2.30 Table 52, §17.2.31 Table 53, §17.2.32
#   Table 54, §17.2.33 Table 55, §17.2.34 Table 56 (+ Appendix A.1 Table 130), §17.2.36 Table 58, §17.2.53 Table 75,
#   §17.2.57 Table 79, §17.2.63 Table 85, §17.2.64 Table 86. TLV codes from the tables match em-types codes.rs:279
#   Upstream (pinned ba4180b, read from an extracted copy): em_steering.cpp:469-498 (0x9b sender: window by plain
#   assignment = host order, timer htons, always one STA and one target even for Request_Mode 0, reserved nibble never
#   written), :500-524 (0x9c sender: 13 octets, Target_BSSID commented out), :527-541 (0xa3 sender), em_base.h:1140-1183
#   port_rule: lines 12 and 15 UPSTREAM (0x9b window little-endian per 0008 D6; 0x9b timer big-endian = upstream
#   htons); every other row SPEC or "-". Note 0009 D2 (raw reserved values, zero counts), D4 (no lenient row in this
#   batch; the 13-octet 0x9c is named a spec form), D5, D8 (zero where the spec says one or more is invalid).
#   Only Table 53 (0x9d Num_STA "Indicates one or more STA(s)") says one or more.
# Byte order of every multi-octet integer (hex = tlvValue only):
#   0x9b Steering_Opportunity_Window: LITTLE-endian (audit 12 UPSTREAM, D6; em_steering.cpp:485 plain assignment).
#   0x9b BTM_Disassociation_Timer: big-endian (audit 15 UPSTREAM, htons at :487; also §3.1.2).
#   0xc3 Steering_Opportunity_Window and BTM_Disassociation_Timer: big-endian (§3.1.2; audit 191 SPEC, no upstream
#     sender, so D6 does not apply). Deliberately different from 0x9b's window.
#   0x9d Validity Period: big-endian (§3.1.2; audit 111, htons/ntohs at em_steering.cpp:79, em_agent.cpp:811).
#   0xc9 Status Code, 0xca Reason_Code: big-endian (§3.1.2; audit 204, 206: htons/ntohs).
#   0x92: STA_MAC(6), AP_MAC(6), octet {AssociationType b7, Reserved b6-0}. Exactly 13.
#   0x9b: BSSID(6), octet {Request_Mode b7, BTM_Disassociation_Imminent b6, BTM_Abridged b5, BTM_Link_Removal_Imminent
#         b4, Reserved b3-0}, Steering_Opportunity_Window(2, LE), BTM_Disassociation_Timer(2, BE), STA_List_Count(1),
#         STA_List_Count x STA_MAC(6), Target_BSSID_List_Count(1), Target_BSSID_List_Count x { Target_BSSID(6),
#         Target_BSS_Operating_Class(1), Target_BSS_Channel_Number(1) }. Both counts may be 0.
#   0xc3: as 0x9b with window and timer big-endian and each target entry { Target_BSSID(6), OpClass(1), Channel(1),
#   0x9c: BSSID(6), STA_MAC(6), BTM_Status_Code(1; raw), Target_BSSID(0 or 6). Value is 13 or 19 octets.
#   0x9d: BSSID(6), Association Control(1; 0x04-0xff reserved, raw), Validity Period(2, BE), Num_STA(1; >= 1), Num_STA x
#   0x9f: MAC_Address(6), Target_BSSID(6), Result_Code(1; 0x02-0xff reserved, raw). Exactly 13.
#   0xa0: Protocol(1; raw, Table 130), Payload(rest of the value, raw, may be empty). At least 1 octet.
#   0xa3: Reason_Code(1; 0x00 and 0x07-0xff reserved, raw), STA_MAC(6, always present). Exactly 7.
#   0xbf: Num_BSSID(1; may be 0), Num_BSSID x { BSSID(6), Status(1; 0x02-0xff reserved, raw) }.
#   0xc9: Status Code(2, BE). Exactly 2.   0xca: Reason_Code(2, BE). Exactly 2.
#   (1) Items are written in the listed order, each at its own position, except the bit-group items of rule (4).
#   (2) Widths: bssid, sta_mac, ap_mac, mac, target_bssid, sK_mac, tK_bssid, bK_bssid are 6-octet MACs (12 hex digits).
#       window and timer (0x9b, 0xc3), validity (0x9d), status_code (0xc9), reason_code (0xca) are 2 octets in the
#       byte order listed above (0x9b window little-endian; all the others big-endian). Every other integer item is
#       1 octet (status, control, op_class, channel, result, protocol, reason, stas, targets, bssids, tK_class,
#       tK_ch, tK_reason, bK_status). Values are decimal or 0x-hex.
#   (3) Count items (stas, targets, bssids) are written as given; only the entries listed follow (a count above the
#       listed entries = overstated). Entries: 0x9b/0xc3/0x9d sK_mac; 0x9b/0xc3 tK_bssid, tK_class, tK_ch (+ tK_reason
#   (4) Bit-field octets: each group is ONE octet, written at the position of the group's first listed item; flag
#       values are 0/1, unshifted; a reserved mask is given in octet position and ORed in (absent = 0):
#       0x92 {assoc b7, event_reserved b6-0}; 0x9b and 0xc3 {req_mode b7, dissoc_imminent b6, abridged b5,
#       link_removal b4, mode_reserved b3-0}. A case that sets a reserved mask: the decoder ignores it, the encoder
#       writes zero (canonical bytes = the *-clear sibling, or the same fields with the mask 0).
#   (5) Byte-string items (0xa0 payload) are hex: raw octets, written exactly as given with no length octet
#   (6) An item given as hex: where it normally takes a MAC or integer is a cut field: exactly those raw octets are
#       written (0x9c target_bssid=hex:.. writes only those octets). An item not listed is absent from the bytes
#   (7) trailing=hex: raw octets appended after the listed fields.
# Choices (for the coordinator): (a) every cut field, partial entry or overstated count is error=Truncated (as
#   B01-B07); extra octets after a complete layout are TrailingBytes. 0x9c Target_BSSID of 1-5 octets is Truncated
#   (cut field); InvalidLength is the alternative reading of "0 or 6 octets". 0x9c of 20+ octets is TrailingBytes.
#   0xa0 has no trailing case (Payload takes the rest). 0xc9/0xca tlvLength is "Variable" but the table has one
#   2-octet field: a third octet is TrailingBytes. (b) 0x9d zero-stas is invalid, error=InvalidLength (Table 53 "one or
#   more", D8; precedent linkmetric zero-links, capability 0xd4 zero-radios). (c) 0x9b/0xc3 opportunity-with-target
#   (Request_Mode 0, Target_BSSID_List_Count 1; "If Request_Mode bit is set to zero, then this field is set to zero")
#   is kind=spec: the counts size the bytes, so it parses as spec bytes (D4: no lenient decoder; meaning is the
#   consumer's). It is upstream's production form for 0x9b (em_steering.cpp:488-493, audit 13). Conflicting
#   precedent: channel group, 0xa6 Fresh=0 with op classes = ValueOutOfRange. If the coordinator picks
#   ValueOutOfRange here, 0x9b opportunity-with-target becomes a lenient candidate with that sender line.
#   (d) targets-not-one-or-stas (STA_List_Count 3, Target_BSSID_List_Count 2; spec "= 1 or STA_List_Count") is
#   kind=spec for the same reason (value rule for the consumer); flagged with (c). (e) mandate-all-stas-one-target
#   (STA_List_Count 0 with one target under Request_Mode 1) is kind=spec. (f) Window and timer are carried in
#   Request_Mode 1 although "ignored" (golden has a non-zero window so its byte order is visible). (g) 0x9b window
#   little-endian vs 0xc3 window big-endian is deliberate (UPSTREAM line 12 vs SPEC line 191); the goldens use the
#   same window value (0x012c) so a shared encoder fails one of them. (h) 0xa3 reason 0x00 (reserved; upstream sends
#   it, audit 123) and any STA_MAC are carried raw (kind=spec); the port encoder writing 0x00 is a consumer question.
#   (i) 0x9d twenty-one-stas pins the difference from upstream's MAX_STA_LIST 20 cap (audit 113).
#   (j) 0xa0 Protocol 0x00 and 0x02-0xff are raw reserved values (Table 130).

# Coordinator correction 2026-11-20 (user decision, 0009 A8): Request Mode 0 with a target list is invalid (ValueOutOfRange) for strict decoding; 0x9b opportunity-with-target is upstream's sender form (em_steering.cpp:488-493) -> kind=lenient, decoded=targets-dropped (the lenient body has no targets); 0xc3 has no production sender -> kind=invalid.
